## Case model

A case is one scenario with one expected outcome and one evidence basis. The importer builds it from the legacy suite structure: every fixture of one suite that shares a shape (or hand-named group), a role (positive base, one-property twin, benign control) and an evidence tier is one case, and each of those fixtures is one projection of it.

| Case type | Cases |
| --- | --- |
| `benign` | 1,537 |
| `cross-family` | 117 |
| `mutation` | 540 |
| `positive` | 388 |
| `twin` | 540 |

| Expected outcome | Cases | Fixtures |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `must-flag` | 382 | 2,399 |
| `must-not-flag` | 1,529 | 3,476 |
| `not-assertable` | 14 | 50 |

| Evidence basis | Cases |
| --- | --- |
| `project-policy` | 785 |
| `provider-documented` | 207 |
| `tool-corroborated` | 919 |
| `unresolved` | 14 |

Wording: 114 cases use hand-written topic, scenario and importance text for a named legacy group (`scripts/migrate/lib/case-narratives.mjs`); 1,811 are worded from role templates plus the family names. Both kinds state the expected outcome in scanner-neutral terms.

## Legacy assessment to canonical expectation

Outcome comes from the legacy assessment kind and, for `policy`, from whether the fixture has expected spans. The basis comes from the tier (T1 `provider-documented`, T2 `tool-corroborated`, T3 `project-policy`, T0 `unresolved`) with the same mechanical tightening as the taxonomy import.

| Legacy kind / tier | Canonical outcome | Fixtures |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `must-not-flag/T0` | `not-assertable` | 19 |
| `must-not-flag/T1` | `must-not-flag` | 10 |
| `must-not-flag/T2` | `must-not-flag` | 2,069 |
| `must-not-flag/T3` | `must-not-flag` | 1,397 |
| `must-redact/T0` | `not-assertable` | 31 |
| `must-redact/T1` | `must-flag` | 1,298 |
| `must-redact/T2` | `must-flag` | 551 |
| `policy/T3` | `must-flag` | 550 |

| Basis change | Cases |
| --- | --- |
| T2 recorded as `project-policy`: cited sources do not include two distinct owners | 138 |
| T1 recorded below `provider-documented`: no cited source is provider-owned | 0 |

T0 fixtures were unscored in the legacy benchmark, so they become `not-assertable` and their candidate spans are dropped. Cases in `unresolved` never carry a must-flag or must-not-flag expectation.

## Coverage of the required scenario themes

Cross-provider themes are `scenarios` tags on cases; a case may carry several.

| Theme | Cases | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cross-provider` | 44 | The case involves credential families of more than one provider. |
| `documentation-placeholder` | 137 | Documentation examples, tutorial defaults and placeholder text that look like credentials but were never issued. |
| `high-signal-assignment-false-positive` | 22 | Values assigned under a credential-sounding name that are nevertheless not secrets, so the name alone must not decide. |
| `partial-span-leakage` | 69 | Credentials embedded in a longer structure, where reporting only part of the value (or only the structure) leaves secret bytes exposed. |
| `templated-reference` | 135 | Template expressions, variable interpolation and secret-manager references that name a secret without containing it. |

Cases involving more than one family are typed `cross-family` (117); 11 cases involve no family and give an `unscopedReason`.

Twin cases carry `relations: [{ type: "twin-of", target, mutationKind }]` to the positive case; each twin fixture carries `lineage.of` to the exact positive fixture and the legacy mutation note. Generated fixtures are never canonical: they record the generator, its source revision and entrypoint, and their cases are the inputs (`origin.type: generation-rule`).

## Historical incidents

| Legacy known-gap data | Count |
| --- | --- |
| known-gap issues read | 63 |
| kind `false-negative` | 38 |
| kind `false-positive` | 25 |
| case incident attachments written | 78 |

Each issue becomes an `incidents[]` entry on every case that owns one of its fixtures: a scanner-neutral failure mode (`false-alarm`, `missed-credential`), the issue title as the summary, the date it was first observed, and the product issue as an `externalRefs` pointer. Product workflow (status, fix commit, promotion, candidate build) and the recorded scanner findings are not imported.

## Dropped, collapsed and lossy

Nothing below is silently lost: each row is a legacy field or fact that the canonical model does not represent, with how many times it occurred.

| Legacy field or fact | Count | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fixture-detectors.json` entries (detector assignments per fixture) | 5,925 | Scanner/product mapping, not evidence. Detector names are never canonical identity. |
| fixture `detectors` (in corpora) | 4,483 | Same as above. |
| fixture `arrivalTargets` | 1,079 | Product arrival-family scoring targets. |
| `assessment.contract` (detector-keyed contract id) | 5,651 | Detector key; the family and its format contract come from the fixture index instead. |
| fixture `expectedAction` (redact/warn) | 124 | Product policy action, not a semantic outcome. |
| fixture `policyFamily`, `policyConformance` | 19 | Product qualification bookkeeping. |
| fixture `formatReason` | 58 | Duplicate of `assessment.reason`. |
| fixture-index `provenance.milestone` / `release` | 3,901 / 1,465 | Product release bookkeeping. |
| `assessment.reason` variants collapsed to the most frequent one per case | 874 | A case has one expectation rationale; the other wordings are per-fixture repetitions (mostly "Negative twin of <fixture>: ..."). |
| T0 fixtures' candidate spans | 31 in 31 fixtures | Unscored and unresolved in legacy; `not-assertable` carries no spans. |
| companion spans on must-not-flag fixtures | 1 | A companion span means "redacting is accepted, never required"; a must-not-flag fixture has no spans in the canonical model. |
| boilerplate span notes | 2,404 | The standard synthetic-value sentence, already implied by the safety rule. |
| assessment sources with no evidence-source record | 68 | Project-owned URLs (`https://github.com/redact-secret/redact-secret/blob/ec9224d9743066fe73d6e61e9843ef52bd853833/docs/decisions/2026-09-24-redact-provider-named-credential-assignments.md`, `https://github.com/redact-secret/redact-secret/issues/948`) that the taxonomy import did not carry. |
| suite `references`, `milestoneReview` | 4 / 1 | Release-review bookkeeping. |
| known-gap product workflow: status (`fixed` / `verified` / `policy-decision`) | 35 / 21 / 7 | Product lifecycle, not evidence. |
| known-gap product workflow: fix, promotion, candidate build, verification, disposition | 56 / 56 / 63 / 21 / 7 | Product workflow and release state. |
| known-gap recorded scanner findings (expected vs actual rows) | 194 | Scanner output is an observation for downstream repositories, never evidence. |
| known-gap fixtures in suites outside the imported set | 37 | Fixtures of legacy suites that are not part of this import (`beta9-external-inputs`); 11 issue(s) have no imported fixture and therefore no incident. |

Also not imported: `supportStatus`, scores and ledger rows (never in these files). Free text is truncated to the 2,000-character schema limit when needed: 0 truncation(s).

## Families

160 of 173 taxonomy families are referenced by at least one case. 13 are not: `atlassian:access-token`, `aws:context-specific-credential`, `aws:sts-service-bearer-token`, `google:oauth2-credential`, `linear:oauth-access-token`, `mistral:realtime-client-token`, `netlify:other-prefixed-tokens`, `npm:legacy-token`, `openrouter:management-api-key`, `slack:workflow-webhook-token`, `vercel:api-key`, `vercel:integration-token`, `voyage-ai:api-key`. They have contracts and sources (#3) but no legacy fixture exercised them.

## Determinism and reproduction

The importer runs the legacy generators (`fixtures/generated/build.mjs`) in a child process over the pinned `git archive`, checks each corpus's SHA-256 against `benchmarks/generated-corpora.json`, and refuses to import on any mismatch. Case ids, ordering and wording are pure functions of that input and of the committed taxonomy records (#3). `npm run migrate:cases:check` regenerates in memory and compares every owned file and this report.
